questions.stem: Which of the following is the ANTONYM of the word 'BENEVOLENT'?

options.option_text: filled with charitable goodwill towards all
bearing malice and ill-will towards others
completely indifferent and detached from others
overly generous in sharing available resources

questions.explanation: BENEVOLENT means wishing well and showing kindness; its antonym is MALEVOLENT — bearing malice or active ill-will. Option C (indifferent) is a common distractor but indifference denotes absence of feeling, not hostile intent, so it is not a precise antonym. Option D is a near-synonym of benevolent.

questions.stem: The director's address was so VERBOSE that the audience lost interest halfway through. The antonym of the highlighted word is best captured by which option?

options.option_text: rambling and filled with needless repetition
brief and expressed in very few words
loud and delivered with great self-confidence
technical and difficult for most to follow

questions.explanation: VERBOSE means using more words than necessary; its antonym is TERSE or LACONIC — brief and using very few words. Option A is a near-synonym of verbose. Options C and D describe delivery style and complexity respectively, neither of which relates to the volume of words used.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the ANTONYM of the word 'INTREPID'?

options.option_text: boldly daring and courageous under pressure
cautious and methodical in every approach
easily frightened and lacking personal courage
recklessly impulsive without any prior plan

questions.explanation: INTREPID means fearless and dauntlessly brave; its antonym is TIMID or CRAVEN — easily frightened and lacking courage. Option B (cautious) is a common exam trap: caution implies prudence, not cowardice, and a cautious person may still be brave. Option D describes recklessness, which is unrelated to the fearless–fearful axis.

questions.stem: The coach remained SANGUINE about the team's prospects despite a string of recent defeats. Which option carries the meaning OPPOSITE to the highlighted word?

options.option_text: cheerfully optimistic about all future outcomes
calm and largely unmoved by changing events
passionately driven and fiercely competitive
gloomy and persistently expecting the worst

questions.explanation: SANGUINE means optimistic, especially in a difficult situation; its antonym is PESSIMISTIC or DESPONDENT. Option B (calm/unmoved) describes the PHLEGMATIC temperament — a separate concept often confused with sanguine. Option A restates the word's own meaning, making it a synonym rather than an antonym.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the ANTONYM of the word 'TACITURN'?

options.option_text: talkative and very fond of long conversation
quiet and reluctant to share personal opinions
secretive and deliberately withholding details
thoughtful and choosing every word with great care

questions.explanation: TACITURN means habitually reserved and saying very little; its antonym is GARRULOUS or LOQUACIOUS — talkative and fond of conversation. Options B and C are near-synonyms of taciturn. Option D is a subtle trap: choosing words carefully suggests thoughtful speech, not necessarily sparse speech, yet many candidates confuse careful diction with taciturnity.

questions.stem: The new trainee was so OBSEQUIOUS towards every senior manager that his colleagues found the behaviour deeply unsettling. The antonym of the highlighted word is best described as which option?

options.option_text: constantly fawning and submissive to authority
boldly self-assured and firmly unyielding
politely formal and respectful in all dealings
eagerly seeking approval and constant validation

questions.explanation: OBSEQUIOUS means excessively eager to serve or please superiors — essentially servile and self-abasing. Its antonym is ASSERTIVE or INDEPENDENT — self-assured and unyielding. Option C (politely formal) is the most tempting distractor because politeness superficially resembles deference; however, formal respect is appropriate behaviour and lacks the self-abasement inherent in 'obsequious'. Options A and D paraphrase the word's own meaning.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the ANTONYM of the word 'PHLEGMATIC'?

options.option_text: slow to react and emotionally unresponsive
deeply melancholic and inclined towards brooding
easily stirred and intensely emotionally volatile
quietly reflective and given to deep thought

questions.explanation: PHLEGMATIC (from classical humours theory) means calm, stolidly unemotional, and difficult to excite; its antonym is EXCITABLE or VOLATILE — easily roused and emotionally unpredictable. Option B (melancholic) is the most dangerous distractor: melancholy is also a humours-theory term and denotes sadness or gloom, not emotional volatility — candidates who know the theory often conflate the two. Option D describes a contemplative, not an excitable, temperament.

questions.stem: Which of the following is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the word 'FRUGAL'?

options.option_text: extremely careful in spending money
spending or giving resources extravagantly
managing household expenses with economy
saving money to prepare for the future

questions.explanation: FRUGAL means thrifty and careful not to waste resources. Its antonym is EXTRAVAGANT or PRODIGAL — spending lavishly without restraint. Options A and C are near-synonyms of frugal (both describe careful spending). Option D (saving for the future) is also a frugal trait, not its opposite.

questions.stem: The meditation retreat offered a SERENE environment that instantly calmed every visitor. Which option is the ANTONYM of the highlighted word?

options.option_text: wildly agitated and emotionally turbulent
perfectly still and completely undisturbed
quiet and composed under great pressure
peaceful and entirely free from worry

questions.explanation: SERENE means calm, peaceful, and untroubled. Its antonym is TURBULENT or AGITATED — wildly disturbed and emotionally restless. Options B, C, and D all describe states of calmness and are synonymous with serene, not opposite to it. Candidates often confuse 'turbulent' with weather alone, but it applies equally to emotional states.

questions.stem: History remembers the minister as PERFIDIOUS — he pledged loyalty to the king while secretly negotiating with the enemy. Which option is the ANTONYM of the highlighted word?

options.option_text: completely devoted and trustworthy in conduct
prone to sudden and unpredictable betrayal
skilled at deception through charming behaviour
guarded and secretive in personal relationships

questions.explanation: PERFIDIOUS means guilty of treachery and betrayal. Its antonym is FAITHFUL or LOYAL — completely devoted and dependable. Options B and C both describe treacherous behaviour and are synonyms of perfidious. Option D (guarded and secretive) is a common distractor because secrecy sounds opposite to openness, but it does not address loyalty or betrayal.

questions.stem: Which of the following is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the word 'ACRIMONY'?

options.option_text: sharp hostility expressed through bitter words
warm and genuinely friendly manner of engagement
deliberate restraint in expressing opinions openly
persistent criticism directed at public figures

questions.explanation: ACRIMONY means bitterness or ill feeling, especially in speech or manner. Its antonym is CORDIALITY or AMIABILITY — a warm, friendly disposition. Option A is a paraphrase of acrimony itself. Option C (restraint in expression) relates to silence, not warmth; Option D (persistent criticism) is a specific form of acrimony, not its opposite.

questions.stem: The new recruit appeared DIFFIDENT during the group discussion, rarely voicing her well-researched opinions. Which option is the ANTONYM of the highlighted word?

options.option_text: lacking confidence and reluctant to speak up
boldly self-assured and socially confident
reluctant to express personal opinions openly
quietly reserved about personal achievements

questions.explanation: DIFFIDENT means modest or shy due to lack of self-confidence. Its antonym is ASSERTIVE or SELF-ASSURED — bold, confident, and willing to speak up. Options A and C directly restate the meaning of diffident. Option D (quietly reserved) is a common trap because reserve can seem like the opposite of aggression, but it still describes diffident-like behaviour.

questions.stem: The professor's lecture was so RECONDITE that even doctoral students struggled to follow the arguments. Which option is the ANTONYM of the highlighted word?

options.option_text: widely known and easily understood by most
requiring specialist expertise to fully grasp
hidden from ordinary understanding and scrutiny
rarely discussed in mainstream academic circles

questions.explanation: RECONDITE means abstruse, known only to a few, little known to general audiences. Its antonym is COMMONPLACE or ACCESSIBLE — widely understood without specialist knowledge. Option B is essentially a synonym (specialist expertise needed = recondite). Option C (hidden from scrutiny) mirrors the obscurity of recondite. Option D (rarely discussed) is also synonymous. Candidates confuse 'accessible' with 'simple', but accessibility of knowledge is the core opposite here.

questions.stem: Which of the following is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the word 'PUSILLANIMOUS'?

options.option_text: exhibiting timid and cowardly behaviour regularly
marked by bold and fearless determination
overly cautious when confronting personal risk
hesitant and indecisive in difficult situations

questions.explanation: PUSILLANIMOUS means showing a lack of courage or resolve; cowardly in spirit. Its antonym is DAUNTLESS or VALIANT — marked by bold, fearless, unwavering determination. Option A is a direct synonym of pusillanimous. Options C and D both describe timid, hesitant behaviour, which is the very essence of pusillanimity, not its opposite. The word derives from Latin 'pusillus' (very small) + 'animus' (spirit), literally 'small-spirited'.
